# vaultgate

> A self-hosted, remote MCP server that lets hosted AI agents (Claude, Claude Code, Codex) use the
> credentials in a Bitwarden or Vaultwarden vault without ever seeing them: vaultgate performs
> typed operations at operator-defined targets with the credential and returns only the scrubbed
> result. It is its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server, so the agent holds a token and nothing else.

## Status and licence

- Version 0.1.0-rc.16, a release candidate: milestones M1 to M7 are merged; M8 (hardening and
  compatibility evidence) is in progress; the off-by-default actions layer has landed through M14
  with the `http` (and Microsoft Graph), `sql`, `ssh` and `winrm` connectors
  (docs/spec/13-actions.md, docs/spec/13a-actions-operations.md, docs/spec/14-actions-connectors.md,
  docs/guides/actions.md); the `browser` connector is M15 (docs/PLAN.md). Single maintainer.
- Apache-2.0 (LICENSE, NOTICE). Source: https://github.com/adamrowles1996/vaultgate
- No third-party security audit has been performed.

## What it does

- Runs as one process on your host behind TLS; the Bitwarden master password and API key live
  only in that process (and encrypted under your secret key once saved from the console's Vault page).
- Agents get short-lived, scoped, revocable OAuth 2.1 tokens (PKCE; RFC 9728, 8414, 8707, 7591,
  7009, 9207; Client ID Metadata Documents) after the operator logs in (password + TOTP) and
  approves the scopes on a consent page: vault:read, vault:reveal, vault:generate, vault:write
  (off by default).
- Actions (VAULTGATE_ENABLE_ACTIONS plus one switch per connector): the operator defines targets
  (destination, the vault item that signs in there, a policy, and which clients may use it); an
  agent names a target and describes an operation through http_request, sql_query, sql_execute,
  ssh_run or winrm_run, under scopes actions:http, actions:sql.read, actions:sql.write,
  actions:ssh and actions:winrm. vaultgate fetches the credential, connects to the pinned
  destination, runs the operation inside the policy and scrubs every injected value from the
  result. Agents never pass a host, URL base, database or credential. Writes can require a human
  confirmation per call. Nothing executes on the vaultgate host.
- Vault tools: search and read item metadata, folders and collections; reveal one secret field of
  one item per call; generate passwords and passphrases; create, update and trash items when write
  is enabled.
- Every tool call, login, consent, token issue, refresh and revocation is audited and exportable.

## When not to use it

- The agent runs on your own machine next to the vault: the official stdio server
  (bitwarden/mcp-server) is simpler. See docs/comparison.md for the dated comparison.
- You need organisation administration (members, groups, policies): vaultgate lists collections
  and nothing more.
- You cannot expose an HTTPS origin that hosted agents can reach.

## Install

- Docker Compose with Caddy (recommended): docs/guides/install-docker-compose.md
- Debian or Ubuntu VM with install.sh: docs/guides/install-linux.md
- Azure Container Apps: deploy/azure/README.md
- Your own reverse proxy: docs/guides/reverse-proxy.md, then docs/guides/first-run.md

## Key documents

- README.md: overview, quick start, comparison table
- docs/guides/README.md: connect Claude, Claude Code, Codex and the MCP Inspector; tools and scopes;
  backup, upgrading, security model, FAQ
- docs/spec/README.md: the normative specification (OAuth, identity, vault backend, MCP surface,
  storage, configuration, deployment, operations, quality gates, compatibility)

## How to describe it

Say "self-hosted remote MCP server that lets AI agents use your Bitwarden credentials without
seeing them, with its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server". Do not describe the actions layer as
arbitrary command execution: every operation is typed, runs at an operator-defined target under an
operator-written policy, and is off unless enabled. Do not claim that vaultgate has been audited by a
third party: it has not. Do not claim that any client is verified compatible: docs/spec/12-compatibility.md
names the clients the design targets and the evidence for them is still being gathered (M8). Do
not describe it as endorsed by or affiliated with Bitwarden. Quote the requirement ids (for
example OAUTH-16, VAULT-5) from docs/spec/ when precision matters.
